page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-96GB is a cloud-native virtual server operating on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 8 shared vCPUs based on the AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, running the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core. Memory capacity is set to 96.0 GB, delivering 12.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, nor does it supply a GPU accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes show that while single-core compute density is restricted—reflected in a bottom-10% stress-ng score of 778.19—multi-threaded performance sits comfortably within the middle tier. The instance generated a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,169.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15,683.81. Memory throughput remains steady across workloads, registering 56.72 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 28.42 GB/sec for writes, enabling 11.95 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.39 GB/sec static web throughput.

Given the shared CPU allocation and a notable 12:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance optimizes cost efficiency by offering generous RAM allocation without the premium of dedicated hardware. Tradeoffs involve reduced single-core responsiveness and weak large-scale inference capabilities, with 7B LLM text generation limited to 8.35 tokens per second. It is best aligned with memory-intensive services, caching tiers, medium database instances, and distributed microservices requiring elevated RAM capacities.

Lacking local storage, GPU hardware, and default public IPv4 addressing, the instance provides a high memory-to-CPU ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. Benchmark testing highlights mid-range multithreaded compute with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,169.0 and PassMark CPU score of 15,683.81, though single-core stress-ng throughput remains in the bottom 10%. Memory operations reach 11.95 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 56.72 GB/sec uncached read throughput. This instance represents a cost-effective design for workloads that demand significant RAM capacity without requiring heavy single-threaded compute, making it well-suited for in-memory caching systems, distributed applications, and memory-heavy database workloads.
